results.name: late_minus_early_yes_rate
results.description: Yes-rate on trials with trial_index above the median minus yes-rate at or below it; the model has no session dynamics, so observed above null means people become more liberal (more yes) later in the session, below means more conservative.

results.name: cell_rate_dispersion
results.description: Variance across (set, target) cells of the cell's yes-rate (each cell has repeated answers); observed above null means the model's per-cell predictions are too flat/undifferentiated (people discriminate cells more sharply), below means the model is too extreme/deterministic across cells.

results.name: single_example_yes_rate
results.description: Yes-rate on trials whose set has exactly one example (target different from it); observed above null means the model still generalizes too narrowly from a single example, below means too broadly.

results.name: inside_range_yes_rate_multi
results.description: Yes-rate for targets strictly inside the [min, max] range of the examples (and not an example) on sets of 2+ examples; observed below null means the model over-fills the gap between examples (people do not treat the range as a contiguous interval as strongly), above means it under-fills.
results.code:
# name: inside_range_yes_rate_multi
# description: Yes-rate for targets strictly inside the [min, max] range of the examples (and not an example) on sets of 2+ examples; observed below null means the model over-fills the gap between examples (people do not treat the range as a contiguous interval as strongly), above means it under-fills.
def test_statistic(df):
    ns = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    parts = ns.str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    n = parts.notna().sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
    lo = parts.min(axis=1).to_numpy(float)
    hi = parts.max(axis=1).to_numpy(float)
    tg = df["target"].to_numpy(float)
    inset = parts.eq(df["target"].astype(float), axis=0).any(axis=1).to_numpy()
    ok = (n >= 2) & (tg > lo) & (tg < hi) & ~inset
    if not ok.any():
        return 0.5
    return float(df["rating"].to_numpy(float)[ok].mean())

results.name: shared_divisor_gap_multi
results.description: On sets of 2+ examples whose gcd is >= 3, yes-rate for (non-example) targets divisible by that gcd minus yes-rate for targets not divisible; observed above null means people use the arithmetic (multiples-of) rule more than the model predicts, below means the model over-weights the rule relative to similarity.
results.code:
# name: shared_divisor_gap_multi
# description: On sets of 2+ examples whose gcd is >= 3, yes-rate for (non-example) targets divisible by that gcd minus yes-rate for targets not divisible; observed above null means people use the arithmetic (multiples-of) rule more than the model predicts, below means the model over-weights the rule relative to similarity.
def test_statistic(df):
    parts = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    n = parts.notna().sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
    arr = parts.fillna(0).to_numpy().astype(np.int64)
    g = np.gcd.reduce(arr, axis=1)
    tg = df["target"].to_numpy().astype(np.int64)
    inset = (arr == tg[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    base = (n >= 2) & (g >= 3) & ~inset
    div = base & (tg % np.maximum(g, 1) == 0)
    nd = base & (tg % np.maximum(g, 1) != 0)
    if not div.any() or not nd.any():
        return 0.0
    y = df["rating"].to_numpy(float)
    return float(y[div].mean() - y[nd].mean())

results.name: multi_example_outside_range_yes_rate
results.description: Yes-rate for targets outside the [min, max] range of the examples on sets of 3-4 examples; observed above null means the model (whose evidence weight grows with set size) generalizes too tightly beyond large example sets, below means too loosely.
results.code:
# name: multi_example_outside_range_yes_rate
# description: Yes-rate for targets outside the [min, max] range of the examples on sets of 3-4 examples; observed above null means the model (whose evidence weight grows with set size) generalizes too tightly beyond large example sets, below means too loosely.
def test_statistic(df):
    parts = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    n = parts.notna().sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
    lo = parts.min(axis=1).to_numpy(float)
    hi = parts.max(axis=1).to_numpy(float)
    tg = df["target"].to_numpy(float)
    ok = (n >= 3) & ((tg < lo) | (tg > hi))
    if not ok.any():
        return 0.5
    return float(df["rating"].to_numpy(float)[ok].mean())

results.name: single_example_distance_corr
results.description: Pearson correlation between yes (0/1) and |target - example| on single-example trials (target != example); observed more negative than null means people's single-example generalization falls off with distance more steeply than the model predicts (model too flat/broad), less negative means the model's similarity gradient is too steep.
results.code:
# name: single_example_distance_corr
# description: Pearson correlation between yes (0/1) and |target - example| on single-example trials (target != example); observed more negative than null means people's single-example generalization falls off with distance more steeply than the model predicts (model too flat/broad), less negative means the model's similarity gradient is too steep.
def test_statistic(df):
    ns = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    one = ~ns.str.contains(",")
    ex = pd.to_numeric(ns.where(one), errors="coerce").to_numpy(float)
    tg = df["target"].to_numpy(float)
    ok = one.to_numpy() & np.isfinite(ex) & (ex != tg)
    if ok.sum() < 3:
        return 0.0
    d = np.abs(tg[ok] - ex[ok])
    y = df["rating"].to_numpy(float)[ok]
    if np.std(d) == 0 or np.std(y) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.corrcoef(d, y)[0, 1])

results.name: target_in_set_yes_rate
results.description: Yes-rate on trials whose target is itself one of the shown examples; the model forces this to ~1, so observed below null means the model over-produces yes for already-seen examples (people are noisier/less certain than any concept-membership account).
